newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on India cancellation talk.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on India cancellation talk.

text.p: Talk that India cancelled a tender for 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat plus profit taking and a slide in most soybean contracts pressured CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
India passed on the tender over the weekend, a trader said. "India did not buy, nobody expected India to buy the wheat, nobody with any sense. Why would you offer wheat into these big reports?"
"India passed on the idea that a new election is coming up," the trader said.
Wheat was firm in early dealings.
The market was higher through much of the session on support from USDA's March plantings report and quarterly stocks report, traders said.
"It's supported by the spring wheat numbers which were a little lower than expected," said Jerry Gidel, grains analyst for Dean Witter.
USDA early Monday said U.S. farmers this year would sow 17.775 million acres to spring wheat, 775,000 acres below analysts' average estimate.
Wheat closed 3-1/4 to five cents per bushel lower, with May down 4-1/4 at $3.97-1/2 a bushel.
Excessive wet weather in the key U.S. Northern Plains spring wheat region including heavy snowpack in the Dakota's led to a cutback in estimates for spring wheat acreage, traders and analysts said.

USDA pegged total U.S. wheat acreage for 1997 at 69.187 million acres, below an average of analysts' estimates for 70.1 million acres. USDA pegged U.S. wheat stocks as of March 1 at 822 million bushels, below the average of analysts' expectations for 827 million acres.
Cargill Inc sold two million bushels of July while Refco Inc and SAK Futures each sold one million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 23,000 contracts, above the 17,179 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, Refco Inc bought 1,000 July $3.90 puts, sold 1,000 July $3.60 puts and sold 1,000 July $4.20 calls, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, below the 12,953 traded Thursday.
